title: Liguria Pumps Run Hot: Self-Service Prices Outpace the National Average
dek: As of September 7, Liguria's petrol stations are charging more than the rest of Italy for both Benzina and Gasolio, capping a steady week-long climb.
body: On September 7, self-service Benzina in Liguria averaged €2.078 per litre and self-service Gasolio €2.201 — both a touch above Italy's national self-service averages of €2.066 and €2.195 respectively. Served-pump prices ran higher still, at €2.239 for Benzina and €2.375 for Gasolio, underscoring how much Ligurian drivers pay for the convenience of full service over self-service.

The trend has been steadily upward: Liguria's self-service Benzina price rose from €2.041 on August 31 to €2.078 by September 7, a climb of nearly four cents per litre in just over a week, with Gasolio following the same upward path. Of the region's 537 registered stations, 489 reported prices in the latest count — a 91% reporting rate that points to an active, well-monitored local network even as prices tick higher.

Numbers like these — pulled fresh for a different Italian region every single day — would be a nightmare to maintain by hand in a spreadsheet.
